help.title: How levels work
help.intro: In the risk modes every place has a level from 1 to 4 in each category: travel, conflict, disasters (with wildfires) and health. All shows the highest of them; the other modes show one.

levels.1: No alert, the governments advise normal precautions, and fewer than 25 deaths in armed violence in 12 months.
levels.2: Governments advise increased caution, or 25+ deaths in armed violence in 12 months, or a WHO outbreak notice in the last 30 days, or a drought alert.
levels.3: Governments advise reconsidering travel to all or part of it, or 100+ deaths in armed violence in 12 months, or a GDACS Orange alert.
levels.4: Governments advise against all travel, or 1,000+ deaths in armed violence in 12 months, or a GDACS Red alert.

help.travel: Travel is the level that at least two of the governments covering a place give (U.S., Canada, the Netherlands, the UK and Germany), or the only one's, so one government alone doesn't set it. A stricter government is named on the card by its flag. The Travel mode shows one government's own levels instead.
help.conflict: Conflict counts the deaths in organized violence that UCDP (Uppsala Conflict Data Program) records: fighting between a government and armed groups, between armed groups, and attacks on civilians, where they happened. A war is a conflict with a government on one side and 1,000 or more deaths in 12 months, wherever it is fought. UCDP's figures are preliminary and come out monthly, a month or two behind.
help.confidence: A level rises as soon as a source reports it. A fall is applied once a later update confirms it, so a level doesn't flicker.
help.news: News activity (GDELT) compares protests and violence in the news with a country's normal week. It is shown as unusual or not, and never sets a level.
help.ours: The levels are this site's summary of the sources, not official levels. Each card links to its source.

1.name: Exercise normal precautions
1.desc: The lowest advisory level. Some safety and security risk exists in any international travel.

2.name: Exercise increased caution
2.desc: Be aware of heightened risks to safety and security.

3.name: Reconsider travel
3.desc: Avoid travel due to serious risks to safety and security.

4.name: Do not travel
4.desc: Greater likelihood of life-threatening risks. The U.S. government may have very limited ability to help.

notes.frenchWestIndies: See also Guadeloupe, Martinique, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Martin.

1.name: Take normal security precautions
1.desc: Take similar precautions to those you would take in Canada.

2.name: Exercise a high degree of caution
2.desc: There are identifiable safety and security concerns, or the situation could change quickly. Be very cautious at all times.

3.name: Avoid non-essential travel
3.desc: Specific safety and security concerns could put you at risk. Think about whether you really need to travel.

4.name: Avoid all travel
4.desc: You should not travel here. Your personal safety and security are at great risk.

1.name: Green: you can travel here
1.desc: There are no special safety risks beyond the usual ones for travel.

2.name: Yellow: be aware of safety risks
2.desc: You can travel here, but there are specific safety risks to be aware of.

3.name: Orange: essential travel only
3.desc: Only travel here if it is necessary. It is not safe to go on holiday.

4.name: Red: do not travel
4.desc: Whatever your situation, do not travel here. It is too dangerous.

notes.svalbard: Svalbard is part of Norway on the map, which shows Norway's own advice.

1.name: No advice against travel
1.desc: The FCDO does not advise against travel to any part of this destination. Read the full advice for local risks and entry rules.

2.name: Essential travel only, to parts
2.desc: The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to some parts of this destination.

3.name: Against all travel to parts
3.desc: The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of this destination (or, rarely, against all but essential travel to the whole of it).

4.name: Against all travel
4.desc: The FCDO advises against all travel to the whole of this destination.

1.name: No travel warning
1.desc: The German Foreign Office has no travel warning for this destination. Read its safety advice for local risks.

2.name: Travel to parts advised against
2.desc: The German Foreign Office advises against travel to some parts of this destination.

3.name: Partial travel warning
3.desc: The German Foreign Office warns against travel to parts of this destination, or advises against travel to all of it.

4.name: Travel warning
4.desc: The German Foreign Office warns against all travel to this destination.
